sentences.text: The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

26. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)

nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

32. The ESI Act has been enacted to provide certain benefits to the employees in case of sickness,
maternity and employment injury and make provisions in respect thereof.

Under this Act,
contribution is made not only by the employee but also by the employer.
The claims made by the employees against the employer, where the relationship of the employer and employee exists, were meant to be governed by the ESI Act alone.
It is only for this reason the object of Section 53 of ESI Act was to save the employer from facing more than one claim in relation to the same accident.

However, present claim petition is specifically filed against driver, owner and insurer of offending vehicle for the accidental injuries suffered by the deceased and these persons or company related to the offending vehicle represent an entirely different set of tort-feasors and cannot claim immunity from their liability to pay compensation with reference to the ESI Act.

Furthermore, the judgment relied upon by learned counsel for the Insurance Company i.e. Hamida Khatoon's Case (supra) does Sribasta Panda vs . Kishan Kumar & Ors. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152333133/

33. In any case, on the facts of present case 167 MV Act is not applicable.
In the present case, the accident took place on a public road and same has no connection with employment in question.
Therefore, in any case, such accident is not covered under the provision of Workman Compensation Act 1923.

34. In fact, broadly, there can be 2-3 possibilities:
Firstly, that a person suffered injury in an accident and not covered under the provision of ESI Act/ Workman Compensation Act.
Secondly, that a person suffered injury in an accident and covered under the provision of ESI Act/ Workman Compensation Act because of his nature of job.
But such accident is not result of employment injury.
Thirdly, that a person suffered injury in an accident and covered under the provision of ESI Act/ Workman Compensation Act because of his nature of job.
And further such accident is result of employment injury.
35. In the considered view of this tribunal applicability of Sec 167 of MV Act comes into operation only under the third category mentioned above.
It is further held that sec. 167 MV Act has no applicability in case of 1st and 2nd Category of injuries mentioned above.

36. Thus, this Tribunal is of the opinion that claim petition MACT No.657/18 Sribasta Panda Vs.
Kishan Kumar & ors.
